bull_bear.body: Priority 1: Organic capex (INR 300 Cr) for capacity expansion; Priority 2: Selective inorganic M&A in value-added/rigging to expand global footprint; Priority 3: Dividend payouts (attractive payout noted by analysts); Debt Strategy: Maintained net cash position, no leverage required for growth.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Geopolitical: Middle East conflict causing project delays and supply chain disruption (900 ton volume impact in Q4); Input Costs: Volatility in steel rod and gas prices (though pass-through mechanism exists); Execution: Delays in customer approvals for plasticated LRPC could slow scale-up; Macro: Trade uncertainties/tariffs in US market.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and disciplined; Emphasized resilience of business model, successful navigation of geopolitical headwinds, and transition from deleveraging phase to growth phase; Focused on absolute EBITDA growth alongside margin expansion.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 20% margin guidance is a structural step-up, not cyclical, driven by the permanent exit from low-margin steel business and the 'One Usha Martin' operating leverage; The company is effectively self-funding its entire growth capex while sitting on net cash, a rare profile in capital-intensive manufacturing; Middle East disruption is viewed as a temporary deferral with massive reconstruction upside once conflict resolves.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Net cash position of Rs. 465 crore as on Jun'26 versus Rs. 332 crore net cash at March'26; net debt series Rs. 124 cr (FY24), Rs. 63 cr (FY25), Rs. -332 cr (FY26), Rs. -465 cr (Jun'26).
- Gross debt held flat at Rs. 146 crore in FY26 and Jun'26 (from Rs. 292 cr in FY24 and Rs. 338 cr in FY25 as extracted); gross debt to equity 0.04x and net debt to equity -0.14x at Jun'26.
- Interest coverage (x) of 23.2 (FY24), 18.8 (FY25), 34.4 (FY26), 48.2 (Jun'26); ROCE (continuing operations) 22.8% / 19.3% / 20.6% / 21.4% and ROE 19.2% / 15.8% / 16.8% / 17.3% across the same periods.
- Operating cash flow before income tax of Rs. 242 crore in Q1 FY27 at 116% of operating EBITDA, versus 94% (FY24), 91% (FY25) and 104% (FY26); free cash flow Rs. 166 / 177 / 457 / 135 crore.
- Net cash gives "the financial strength to continue investing in future growth"; the deck discloses no dividend policy or buyback.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- "Established in the year 1960, Usha Martin is a leading global and India's No. 1 specialty steel wire rope solutions provider", also making high-quality wires, low relaxation prestressed concrete steel strand (LRPC), bespoke end-fitments, accessories and related services.
- Diversified end-market exposure: end-industry segmentation for Q1 FY27 is Engineering 23%, Oil & Offshore 21%, Crane 17%, Construction & Infrastructure 9%, Elevator 9%, Auto 7%, Mining 5%, Fishing 3%, Utilities 2%, Others 4%.
- Geographically spread: India 43%, Europe 27%, Asia Pacific 12%, Middle East & Africa 9%, Americas 9%; "The share of international business stood at 57% in Q1 FY27."
- Globally recognised certifications and licences cited: ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015, ISO 45001:2018, DGMS approval, API Certificate of Authority, ABS Manufacturing Assessment, NABL testing (ISO/IEC 17025:2017) and Lloyd's Approved Manufacturer of Steel Wire Rope.
- Long-term issuer rating upgraded by India Ratings and Research Pvt. Ltd. to "IND AA-/Stable", with "IND A1+" reaffirmed for Short-Term Credit Facilities (last review July'26).
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Discontinued business] The P&L shows "Profit/loss from discontinuing business" of Rs. -7.1 crore in Q4 FY26 and nil in Q1 FY27, and EBITDA/ton is stated as "Excluding UM Cables", indicating UM Cables sits outside continuing operations.
- [Joint ventures] Consolidated P&L carries "Share of profit(-)/loss(+) of joint ventures" of -5.0 in Q1 FY27 versus -4.5 in Q1 FY26 and -4.5 in Q4 FY26 (Rs. crore).
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June 2026: Promoters 40%, Institutional Investor 29%, Corporate Bodies 11%, Public including Employee Welfare Trust 20%.
- [Listing] Listed on BSE (517146), NSE (USHAMART) and the Societe de la Bourse de Luxembourg (Scrip Code US9173002042).
- [Geopolitics] Middle East rope volumes reduced "caused by the ongoing geopolitical conflict", offset by India, US and Europe.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: Q4 Margin 21.6% driven by: 1) Product mix shift to high-value ropes (crane, mining, elevator); 2) 'One Usha Martin' savings (INR 65-70 Cr annualized: fixed employee costs -3%, admin -7%); 3) Full pass-through of input cost inflation (steel, gas); Cost Headwinds: LPG/Propane costs doubled (INR 60k to INR 120-130k/ton), impacting INR 2.5-3 Cr/month; Mitigation: 25% fuel switch to natural gas completed.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: 10-12% volume CAGR expected for next 2-3 years; Margin: Minimum 20% operating margin benchmark (vs prior 18-19%); Order Inflow: Strong visibility for H1 FY27, especially in value-added segments; Capex/Commissioning: INR 300 Cr over next 2 years for elevator rope capacity (+6,000 tons), specialized wires, and plasticated LRPC expansion.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Management declined specific quantification but cited 'fairly healthy order book' for specialized projects and strong visibility for H1 FY27; 85% of business is replacement market providing stable baseline; Order inflow accelerating in oil & offshore, crane, and mining segments.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Plasticated LRPC: Approvals imminent (weeks), targeting scale-up from 2,500 tons to 4,000-6,000 tons annually; Synthetic Slings: Gaining traction with repeat orders; Parvatmala Project: Significant rope demand expected in 2-3 years as projects reach final stages; Thailand Plant: Modernization ongoing (18-month timeline) to produce specialized elevator/gondola cords; Market Share Expansion: Sub-5% in US and 10-12% in Europe offer runway for growth.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Usha Martin delivered record Q4 margins (21.6%) and turned net debt to net cash (INR 332 Cr) by shifting mix to high-value ropes and executing cost synergies, positioning the debt-free balance sheet to fund INR 300 Cr capex for 10-12% volume CAGR despite temporary Middle East headwinds.

open.item: The Board has recommended a dividend of Rs. 3.75 per equity share of face value Re. 1 each for FY 2025-26, in accordance with the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy and subject to shareholder approval at the ensuing AGM.

The Company is expanding capacity at its Ranchi facility with a focus on value-added products, to address demand opportunities in construction, elevators, power transmission, bridges, offshore, oil and gas, mining and heavy lifting.
The Company will strengthen its portfolio through customised and value-added products, with greater emphasis on higher-margin segments with lower competitive intensity.

The Company is optimising its manufacturing network and gradually increasing production in India to capture cost efficiency and local capabilities, while integrating global operations and strengthening the supply chain.
The Company intends to invest approximately Rs. 200-250 Crore annually to further expand capacity in high-growth segments such as elevators, cranes and mining.
Expansion at the Ranchi facility is expected to support growing demand across infrastructure, mining, offshore and industrial applications.

Management will push to convert capability into approvals, approvals into orders and orders into repeat business, in order to lift the utilisation of recently commissioned capacity and broaden the customer base it serves.
Management believes meaningful capital can be released from working capital through better forecasting, planning and collection discipline.

The Company will deploy capital judiciously where it sees a clear customer opportunity, a sustainable competitive advantage and attractive long-term returns, and will hold back where those conditions are not met.

Beyond the core wire rope business the Company is building chosen adjacencies — value-added automotive, transmission-line and rockfall protection wires, plasticated LRPC strand for bridge and stay-cable projects, and OceanFibre synthetic slings for offshore and marine applications.

Management's focus is to improve the pace at which capability becomes approvals, approvals become orders and orders become repeat business, which will lift the utilisation of recently commissioned capacity and broaden the customer base it serves.

The Company is integrating its global operations, streamlining processes and strengthening its supply chain, while gradually shifting more production to India for cost efficiency and local capabilities.

The move from net debt to net cash gives the Company flexibility to invest in capacity, technology, product development and market expansion, with capital to be deployed judiciously only where there is a clear customer opportunity, a sustainable competitive advantage and attractive long-term returns.

risks.note: Ongoing global conflicts, particularly in West Asia, and disruptions in key trade routes such as the Strait of Hormuz may impact supply chains, logistics costs and availability of raw materials for a business that runs long global supply chains.

Changes in global trade policies, including tariff measures and protectionist trends, may affect export competitiveness and market access in key geographies — material given the scale of the Company's international business.
Competition from low-cost manufacturers, especially from East Asian countries, continues to exert pressure on pricing and margins in certain product segments.
Increasing environmental and safety regulations across the markets served may lead to higher compliance costs and operational complexities.

Steel wire and rope production is inherently energy intensive. Limited green energy availability and high adoption costs may hinder decarbonisation, straining operational efficiency, escalating production expenses and delaying sustainability goals; tightening environmental regulation, evolving carbon pricing and the physical risk of extreme weather events affecting manufacturing continuity add further urgency.
risks.risk: Climate stewardship and energy transition (BRSR material issue, negative financial implication)

risks.note: Manufacturing processes generate air pollutants (PM, SOx, NOx). Non-compliance with permissible limits could trigger operational disruptions, regulatory penalties or licence revocations and damage reputation, while lagging global sustainability expectations may lead to financial losses and competitive disadvantage.
Exports contributed 35% of the entity's total turnover, so demand, tariff and currency conditions in overseas markets bear directly on the business.

Manufacturing of wire rope, wire and strands including locked coil accounted for 94.56% of the entity's turnover, leaving performance tied to one product family and its end-market cycles (wire rope alone 63.88%, wire and strands 17.13%, LRPC strand 13.55% of turnover).
